chapter: Records, rivals and New Orleans bands
title: Sunday band battles on the streets of New Orleans
summary: Punch recalls thirty bands on trucks, battles with Sam Morgan, and Buddy Petit's rich tone; winners were judged by hall attendance.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh, it just like Buddy Petit playing. If he would have been a high note fellow boy, he'd have been a killer dealer. But his tone was so rich man. He had a bigger tone than Louis. Boy, there was some days though, brother. I don't see nothing here now like it. Well, Paul, every Sunday, them must have had about thirty bands in the oil, thirty or thirty-five. Well, them band was one at the lake. They was out there on trucks and things, advertising for dancers and things, see. And if the two meet on the corner, there was a ball there that evening, right out in the street. And policemen, there was a ball there, nothing like that. People out there dancing. This band played a tune. That band played a tune. This band played a tune. Then sometimes three of them get up there. And one guy put a chain around our wheel, and the other guy, Sam Morgan wheel. Boy, it was some fun. They don't see that kind of stuff. I mean all day Sunday in the street, just jam and pack with people. It was fun.
Well what about Sam Morgan and you, who won that battle? Who won that battle? One of those corners? Yeah, between you and Sam Morgan.

Well, all the people giving this dance, say they had to go there to round to make. There always something like that come up, you know, or you had to let them go, see. But if you ain't got no round to make, the people out there give you the most applause, well that's the one winning. And how you tell you win, by your hall that night. See, like I'm playing at Economy, playing at Carborette, playing at Family, playing at Santa, different halls, you know. Well if my hall packed and jammed that night, I must have laid sand on the street. That's the only pity you get for it.
